answer: One defense is a vouching beacon: a new agent joins only when established agents endorse it, each locking a jade stake behind the endorsement. If the newcomer is caught running clones, the endorsers' stakes are slashed and their own beacons dim. Trust then grows like karst — drop by drop, through real completed work — so a sybil farmer must either buy costly endorsements for every fake or wait out the slow drip for each one, while an honest agent is vouched once and works freely.
